name: toupas
description: Publish websites and small apps from a chat to a public link anyone can open.

interface.shortDescription: Put websites live at a link
interface.longDescription:
Toupas is a website and small app hosting service. It publishes what you make in ChatGPT to a public link that anyone can open, with no servers or setup.

What you can do:
- Publish a website from a chat and get its link
- Update a live website later, from any conversation
- Publish small apps that save data and have sign-in, such as RSVP lists, trackers and members areas
- Add your own photos and logo
- Check an app's saved data and problems
- Choose who can sign up to an app, and invite people
- Give a website its own name or connect your own domain
- Take a website offline and start it again

Who it's for: anyone who wants a website or small app online without learning about hosting, including small businesses, event organizers and people building their first project.

Limitations: you need a Toupas account. Apps made from a chat can't run custom server code, so they can't take payments, receive webhooks, hold secret keys or run scheduled jobs.
defaultPrompt: Make me a website for my bakery and put it live with Toupas

positive.description: Publish a new website from a chat and get a public link.
positive.prompt: Make a one-page website for a bakery called Review Bakery, with its opening hours, and put it live with Toupas.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT writes the page, publishes it and replies with a toupas.app link. Opening the link shows the Review Bakery page.

positive.description: Update a live website. Run this after the first test case.
positive.prompt: On my Review Bakery website, change the opening hours to 8am to 6pm.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT reads the current page, then publishes the change. The same link now shows 8am to 6pm, and the rest of the page is unchanged.

positive.description: Publish a small app that saves data, with access rules.
positive.prompt: Make an RSVP app with Toupas for a birthday party. Guests give their name and whether they're coming, and only I can see the full list.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT publishes the app, replies with its link and explains who can do what. Opening the link shows the RSVP form.

positive.description: List the websites in the account and whether they're live.
positive.prompt: Which websites do I have on Toupas, and are they live?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT lists the account's websites with their links and whether each is live. Nothing is changed.

positive.description: Take a website offline after the user agrees. Run this after the first test case.
positive.prompt: Take my Review Bakery website offline.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT first says what will happen and asks the user to agree, and the website stays live until then. After the user agrees, the link stops working.

negative.description: An unrelated question. Toupas should not be called, and ChatGPT should answer normally.
negative.prompt: What's a good recipe for sourdough bread?

negative.description: The user wants to see code but not publish it. Nothing should be published.
negative.prompt: Write the HTML for a simple landing page and show it here. Don't put it online.

negative.description: Something Toupas apps can't do. ChatGPT should say plainly that apps made from a chat can't take payments, and shouldn't publish an app that collects card details.
negative.prompt: Make me an online shop with Toupas that charges credit cards and saves the card numbers.

publication.release_notes: First release: publish websites and small apps from ChatGPT to a public link, update them later, and manage whether they're online.
